identity.title: Molecular Reconnaissance of the β Pictoris Gas Disk with the SMA: A Low HCN/(CO+CO<SUB>2</SUB>) Outgassing Ratio and Predictions for Future Surveys

paper_type_evidence.quote: We here present a molecular survey of the $\beta$ Pictoris belt with the Submillimeter Array (SMA), reporting upper limits for CN, HCN, HCO$^+$, N$_2$H$^+$ and H$_2$CO, as well as for H$_2$S, CH$_3$OH, SiO and DCN from archival ALMA data.

question.value: Which molecules other than CO are present in the exocometary gas disk of beta Pictoris, and what do the upper limits imply for the HCN/(CO+CO2) outgassing ratio and for future surveys?

findings_qualitative.value: Only CO is detected; non-detections of other molecules are explained by rapid photodissociation in the strong UV field; CN is the longest-lived after CO.

evidence.quote: CN is the longest-lasting and most easily detectable molecule after CO in this environment.

evidence.quote: finding it plays a key role in CO and CN excitation

claims.hypothesis: Can molecules other than CO be detected in the beta Pic gas disk?

evidence.quote: There are no significant detections of any molecular lines other than CO.

why_this_method.value: Spectro-spatial filtering with CO template maximizes S/N by removing noise-dominated pixels/channels

evidence.quote: This maximizes the signal-to-noise ratio by effectively removing noise-dominated pixels/channels.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CN destruction by atomic oxygen (timescale ~3 yr) neglected due to uncertain O abundance

evidence.quote: Given the uncertainty on the oxygen abundance, however, we opt to neglect this destruction pathway of CN in this work.

limitations_admitted.value: Predictions assume LTE and CO-like distribution; OH prediction sensitive to temperature and spatial distribution.

evidence.quote: our prediction is very sensitive to the choice of OH temperature or spatial distribution, which may be oversimplified here
